entries.title: Fixed dollar-figure text corrupting meta tags on matter/record pages
entries.why: audit.json's weakDescription list (10 pages) included 7 matter pages with implausibly short char counts (live-137: 2, live-203: 11). `grep -rl 'content="[^"]*<meta ' matters/ chapter-11/ federal-cases/` found 31 published pages where a second <meta name="description" content="..."> fragment was spliced into the first one's attribute value. Root cause: build_matter_pages.ts/build_record_pages.ts build title/description/OG/Twitter/canonical tags with .replace(regex, templateString) using a literal "$1" to reinsert the matched opening tag; "$1" is special to String.replace, so a summary containing a dollar figure like "$170M" has its digit read as a second backreference. This was backlog item 5's real cause, not thin content.

verdict.note: Confirmed same-day: the prerender workflow rebuilt all matter/record pages from the fixed builder (commit 0c21e23) within minutes of the push. Live site_audit.py: weakDescription 10 -> 3, and the 3 remaining are exactly the pages flagged as a separate, still-open issue (contact.html, handbook-success.html, reset-password.html), not this fix's targets. Judged now rather than at checkAfter since the result was already unambiguous.

entries.why: imp-004's verdict named contact.html (37 chars), handbook-success.html (65 chars) and reset-password.html (46 chars) as genuinely thin hand-written descriptions, separate from the builder bug -- backlog item 5's still-open remainder. contact.html is indexable (no noindex), so its thin description had real SEO/SERP-snippet impact; the other two are noindex but still read truncated/generic when shared or inspected. Replaced each with copy drawn from the page's own actual content (contact page's real pitch: evaluate the tracker for your team or flag a matter; handbook-success's real coverage: all 50 states + DC, access unlocked on the matching account; reset-password's real flow: new password saved, signed in automatically), 120-152 chars each, within site_audit.py's 70-320 char window.

entries.title: Analyzed why v4.3 misses the final-outcome range 47% of the time; wrote evidence and proposed prompt changes to ops/calculator-proposals.md (NEEDS JEFF)
entries.why: ops/metrics/goals.json (2026-10-15): calculator is the goal furthest behind (gap 0.646, finalRangeHitRate 0.531/target 0.75, calculatorViews7 0/target 50) and untouched by the last 2 log entries (imp-009 traffic, imp-010 conversion); audit was clean. Backlog G3. The valuation method can't be changed from this session (CLAUDE.md) and no change can be deployed from the cloud, so per the playbook's calculator scope this replayed the already-scored, already-published v4.3 backtest results (js/backtest-results-data.js, no new API calls or spend) to find the actual miss pattern rather than guessing. Found two dominant, case-cited patterns across the 15/32 misses: (1) a one-sided party figure (loan principal, punitive prayer, a second rent claim) priced at high confidence as if it directly equalled the award, with no issue modeling the legal theory that actually capped recovery (donegal-v-christie-scott 80x over, can-iv-packard-square 1.6x over, wheeler-reit 2x+ over, 1700-market-v-common-grounds 14x over); (2) in dueling-valuation disputes, when only one side's appraisal figure gets quoted into the record the existing competing-figures basis never triggers and the range anchors to one side only (kks-properties, elpa-builders miss this way; hrt-enterprises, state-v-skyway capture both sides and hit). Two smaller findings (immaterial-issue floor creep on near-exact hits; undercounted multi-claim cases) are documented too. This is evidence plus a proposal, not a code change -- nothing in the calculator's prompt or math was touched.
entries.metric: none directly -- this did not change the live site or the valuation method; what to check next time is whether Jeff has reviewed ops/calculator-proposals.md and ruled on the proposed prompt changes
